answer: A practical defence is to make each agent's reputation costly to rebuild: require a verifiable history of useful work before it can trade at full trust. New identities start at the edge of the network, like a single vertex with no edges, and must earn connections over time. A flood of fresh accounts then looks like a rising tide with no depth - many names, no track record - while a long-lived agent accumulates a jade-clear record of completed tasks, payments and peer endorsements. Forging that history at scale costs more than it gains, so sybils stay marginal.
